stories.headline: S&P 500, NASDAQ HIT RECORD HIGHS AS SPACEX IPO CONFIRMED FOR JUNE 12
stories.body: The S&P 500 rose 0.60% to 7,518 and the Nasdaq surged 1.08% to 26,628, both setting all-time highs on the first trading day after the Memorial Day weekend. SpaceX confirmed a June 12 Nasdaq listing under SPCX at a $1.75 trillion target valuation — which would shatter Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO record and instantly rank among the ten most valuable companies on earth.

stories.headline: IRAN DEAL OPTIMISM SENDS OIL DOWN 2.4%, DOLLAR SLIPS TO 99
stories.body: WTI crude fell 2.37% to $94.31 as Qatari mediators flew into Tehran coordinating with the U.S. to advance a ceasefire that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The DXY dollar index slipped to ~99.2, pulling back from six-week highs. Markets are pricing in lower energy costs and reduced near-term inflation pressure if a deal materializes.

stories.headline: WORKDAY BEATS ESTIMATES; QUALCOMM UP 50%+ SINCE APRIL EARNINGS
stories.body: Workday shares jumped ~4% after the HR/finance software firm posted stronger-than-expected Q1 results and raised its full-year margin outlook. Qualcomm has rallied over 50% since its April 29 earnings — both signal resilient enterprise software and semiconductor demand even as macro uncertainty persists.

stories.headline: HEALTH CARE SECTOR ON TRACK FOR BEST WEEK IN MORE THAN SIX MONTHS
stories.body: The S&P 500 health care sector climbed 3.4% for the week heading into Tuesday's session, its strongest weekly run in over half a year. The rally reflects earnings beats from major insurers and pharma names, plus rotation into defensive sectors as the 10-year yield holds above 4.5% and growth multiples compress.

stories.headline: MICHIGAN WINS 2026 NCAA TITLE; PLAYERS ERA 16 BRACKETS REVEALED
stories.body: Michigan beat UConn in the national championship game, dominating in the paint to secure the Wolverines' title. Off the court, the Players Era 16 tournament bracket was revealed — 24 teams, two Las Vegas events in November, and the largest regular-season event format in college basketball history. Duke tops Andy Katz's first 2026-27 Power 44 rankings.

stories.headline: KNICKS REACH FINALS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 1999; THUNDER HOST SPURS TONIGHT
stories.body: New York swept Cleveland in the Eastern Conference Finals to reach the NBA Finals for the first time since 1999. In the West, OKC hosts San Antonio in Game 5 tonight at 8:30 PM ET — Thunder lead the series 3-1 and are one win from their first Finals appearance. Tip-off is past brief generation time; result pending.

stories.headline: AARON RODGERS CONFIRMS FINAL NFL SEASON; RAMS LOCK UP STAFFORD AT $55M
stories.body: The 42-year-old Rodgers returned to Steelers OTAs and confirmed this is his final season. Meanwhile, the Rams signed Matthew Stafford to a $55M/year extension through 2027. The Seahawks — defending Super Bowl LX champions — are also running OTAs, with a 2026 schedule featuring six primetime games and a rematch against New England on Sept. 9.

stories.headline: 2026 TRANSFER PORTAL WINDOW CLOSES; TOP MOVES RESHAPE POWER FOUR ROSTERS
stories.body: The portal window formally shut last week. Top moves: QB Sam Leavitt to Lane Kiffin's LSU, WR DeAndre Moore Jr. to Colorado (reuniting with Deion Sanders), and five-star WR Quincy Porter from Ohio State to Notre Dame. Washington's staff heads out on 2027 recruiting visits this week after spring ball concluded with Purple beating Gold 27-10.

deepDive.title: The SpaceX IPO: Why 110x Revenue Demands a New Valuation Framework
content: SpaceX's confirmed June 12 Nasdaq listing — targeting a $1.75 trillion valuation on $18.67 billion in 2025 revenue — is not a conventional IPO. If it prices at target, SPCX would instantly rank among the ten most valuable publicly traded companies on earth, eclipsing Tesla's current market cap and raising more than double Saudi Aramco's record 2019 offering. Yet the company posted a $4.9 billion net loss last year. The question for serious equity analysts isn't whether SpaceX is impressive — it's what framework can possibly justify a 110x trailing-revenue multiple.

Traditional DCF analysis breaks down because SpaceX bundles three structurally different businesses under one ticker. First, a government contractor: NASA and DoD launch contracts generate reliable but margin-capped cash flows. Second, a commercial infrastructure monopoly: Starlink crossed 10 million subscribers in 2025, with its connectivity segment posting $1.19 billion in quarterly profit — structurally similar to AWS inside Amazon. Third, an asymmetric moonshot: Starship and the Mars program generate no current revenue but embed the $1+ trillion option premium in the multiple. If Starlink is valued standalone at 8-10x revenue, it implies $400B+ in value alone. The remaining $1.35 trillion is a bet on reusable heavy-lift dominance.

The best historical analog isn't Saudi Aramco — it's Amazon in 2001. Amazon was widely understood to be building indispensable commerce infrastructure while burning capital aggressively, trading at multiples that only worked if you believed in the terminal business. Amazon's peak 2001 price-to-sales was roughly 3x; SpaceX is at 110x. That gap is either the cost of genuine asymmetric optionality in space infrastructure, or the most expensive growth bet in market history. What distinguishes SpaceX from a typical loss-making tech bet: Starship has demonstrated reusability at scale, Starlink has a defensible hardware moat, and no competitor is within a decade of matching the launch cadence.

For today's market setup, the IPO matters beyond SPCX itself. A $75 billion capital raise is a meaningful liquidity event — large IPOs historically cause short-term rotation out of speculative growth names, similar to the pressure Facebook's 2012 listing placed on the Nasdaq for several weeks post-debut. The second variable is the 10-year yield at 4.51%: at that discount rate, cash flows projected 20+ years out — Starship at scale, Mars infrastructure — are worth dramatically less than at pre-2022 levels. Bulls need rates to fall materially for the outer-year SpaceX thesis to hold. Watch the June 11 institutional book — if demand lets Musk upsize the deal, that's the clearest signal yet about how much risk appetite remains in this market.
